text:
kai: Quick note — the new example app next-llama-eval (examples/next-llama-eval) is intermittently failing in our local eval harness when run with CONCURRENT=4. Repro: checkout repo, npm i, RW_API_KEY set to a rotating test key, run `npm run test:eval -- --concurrent=4`.

lina: what's the symptom? 401, 429, or timeouts?

kai: a mix. Mostly timeouts on generate and occasional 401s on embed if the harness injects a simulated KMS rotation. Stack traces point to our minimal HTTP shim used in server handlers. Snippet from their server handler:
```js
export default async function handler(req, res) {
  const payload = { prompt: req.body.prompt };
  const r = await fetch(`${process.env.RW_API_URL}/v1/generate`, {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${process.env.RW_API_KEY}` },
    body: JSON.stringify(payload),
  });
  if (!r.ok) return res.status(r.status).send(await r.text());
  res.json(await r.json());
}
```

lina: aha. That bypasses the SDK which contains retry+refresh logic and hooks into our circuit-breaker. These minimal shims are great for teaching but dangerous as a default.

omar: we intentionally made the sandbox minimal to reduce deps for newcomers. But the tradeoff is onboarding friction when they hit auth/rotation edge cases. We should change the sample to default to SDK-backed calls on server-side routes and keep raw fetch behind a feature flag.

krachel: +1. Also the eval harness should include a deterministic failure test that simulates a rotation: msw or a tiny mock that returns 401 for the first request and 200 for the second. That guarantees the SDK's single-refresh behavior is exercised.

kai: filed GH issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/next-llama-eval/issues/7 — includes CI logs and a tiny repro script. Proposed fix: switch server handlers to use @redwood/sdk-js clients (textClient.generate / embedClient.embed), add REDWOOD_USE_RAW_FETCH=false default, and expose REDWOOD_SDK_RETRIES env var.

lina: implementation detail: SDK exposes retry config but defaults are different across languages. JS default is attempts: 1 refresh on 401 with exponential backoff; Python currently does two refreshes and treats 429 as refreshable. We should standardize defaults and make the SDKs configurable via env to avoid surprising sample behavior.

omar: for the sample patch, can we also add a lightweight telemetry label on each call? Something like `sample.app/{route}:{stage}` so Console can differentiate generate vs embed vs auth-failure. Right now the sample emits only `sample.request` and it's impossible to triage.

krachel: yes please. Add event fields: `component: 'next-llama-eval'`, `stage: 'generate'|'embed'`, `result: 'ok'|'401'|'timeout'|'5xx'`. That will help correlate harness flakes with auth rotations.

lina: one more onboarding improvement: update docs/getting-started.md with a small section "Server-side SSR and tokens" explaining cold-starts, concurrent requests, and recommended patterns (use server-side SDK client, avoid baking ephemeral tokens into container startup scripts). Add a troubleshooting bullet: "If you see intermittent 401s under concurrent SSR, try REDWOOD_USE_RAW_FETCH=false or bump REDWOOD_SDK_RETRIES to 2 for staging runs."

kai: adding a CI-only test too: run the eval harness 10x in a loop with CONCURRENT=4 to catch flakiness early. We'll gate the change behind a feature-flag in CI so it doesn't slow down normal runs.

omar: long-term, we should add a small integration test in the SDK repo that reproduces KMS rotation semantics so all sample apps share the same expectations. I can file a cross-repo ticket.

infra-bot: CI queued for branch kai/sdk-server-default (job 6124).

krachel: PR created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/next-llama-eval/pull/32 — switches server handlers to SDK, adds REDWOOD_USE_RAW_FETCH env flag, exposes REDWOOD_SDK_RETRIES, includes msw-based test for 401->200 rotation, and updates README.

lina: running the changed harness locally with the SDK path fixed our flakes in 20 runs. With raw fetch it still flakes.

kai: merging after CI green. Also adding a short note in the dev-examples README explaining why the SDK is preferred for server-side handlers.

infra-bot: CI passed. Merge complete. Deploy to staging sample registry.

omi: small follow-up — let's also put a one-liner in the Quickstart: "Prefer SDK clients for server-side calls to inherit retry/refresh/circuit-breaker behavior." That should reduce support tickets from new users.

kai: agreed. Closing the GH issue after 48h of no regressions. Thanks team.
